answer: An agent economy can deter sybils by requiring each account to stake funds before submitting jobs or claiming rewards. When linked accounts commit provable fraud, the protocol slashes their stakes and compensates victims. A hundred aliases then mean a hundred deposits at risk, not a hundred free votes. This cannot prove one identity per person, but forces attackers to lock capital and lose it if caught, even when a gale of fake accounts threatens an oasis and trust falls to its nadir.
